newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs sell stdy-off $0.50-private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs sell stdy-off $0.50-private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Tuesday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, with weakness again tied to slaughter cutbacks by packers fighting unprofitable operating margins, livestock dealers said.
Many pork plants were operating at reduced hours for the third consecutive week.
Despite smaller slaughter, cash hog prices were seen steady at some locations on tight hog supplies as farmers continued to focus more on planting and less on hog sales.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 lower at $54.50-$55.00 in the country and $55.50-$56.50 at plants.

Illinois hogs sold steady to firmer at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and up to $56.00 at plants, with some packers paying premiums of $2.00 over Monday's posted USDA top of $56.00 for top quality hogs, sources there said. Supplies were tight as farmers worked feverishly to get as much planting done as possible before rain moves in later Tuesday.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower at $53.50 to $54.00 in the country and $55.50 to $56.50 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said. Ohio hogs sold steady at $52.00 to $53.00 in the country and $54.00 to $55.00 at plants, sources said.
